prompt: In Experiment 1, which of the following was the independent variable (the variable the experimenters deliberately changed)?

choices.rationale: The electrical load connected was kept the same in every trial (a controlled variable).

choices.text: The power output of the turbine
choices.rationale: The power output of the turbine was measured as the outcome (the dependent variable).
Correct. The wind speed was the variable the experimenters deliberately changed (the independent variable).
The color of the blades is not part of the procedure and plays no role in the experiment.

explanation: The procedure changes the wind speed from trial to trial and records the power output of the turbine in response, so the wind speed is the independent variable.

table.caption: Experiment 1: Engineers mounted a small wind turbine in a wind tunnel and measured its electrical power output at several steady wind speeds. The turbine faced directly into the wind in every trial. Table 1 lists the results.

prompt: Which quantity was measured as the result of each trial in Experiment 1?

choices.rationale: Correct. The salinity of the water was measured as the outcome (the dependent variable).
The color of the ship is not part of the procedure and plays no role in the experiment.
The depth below the surface was the variable the experimenters deliberately changed (the independent variable).
The time of day was kept the same in every trial (a controlled variable).

explanation: The salinity of the water is what the experimenters measured after setting the depth below the surface, so it is the dependent variable.

stimulus.title: Ocean Salinity and Depth
stimulus.text:
Experiment 1
From a research ship, scientists lowered a probe that measures salinity on a cable and recorded the salinity at several depths. All readings were taken within one hour.
Results (the salinity of the water): at 100 m, 33.94 g/kg; at 200 m, 34.33 g/kg; at 300 m, 34.55 g/kg; at 400 m, 34.67 g/kg.

prompt: In Experiment 1, which of the following is a controlled variable, kept the same in every trial?

choices.rationale: Correct. The time allowed for dissolving was kept the same in every trial (a controlled variable).

choices.text: The mass of salt that dissolved
choices.rationale: The mass of salt that dissolved was measured as the outcome (the dependent variable).
The temperature of the water was the variable the experimenters deliberately changed (the independent variable).
The shape of the beaker is not part of the procedure and plays no role in the experiment.

explanation: Only the temperature of the water was varied and only the mass of salt that dissolved was measured; the time allowed for dissolving was kept the same so it could not affect the results.

table.caption: Experiment 1: Students heated 100 g of distilled water to a set temperature in a beaker and added the salt one gram at a time, stirring after each addition, until no more would dissolve. They recorded the total mass dissolved at each temperature. Table 1 lists the results.

prompt: The trial at an antibiotic concentration of 0 µg/mL was most likely included in Experiment 1 in order to:

choices.text: Serve as a control against which the other trials could be compared
choices.rationale: Correct. A zero trial shows what happens with none of the treatment, so the effect of each nonzero amount can be judged against it.

choices.text: Check that the instrument used to measure the number of colonies was properly calibrated
choices.rationale: Nothing in the procedure uses the zero trial to calibrate an instrument.

choices.text: Determine whether the volume of culture spread on each plate has any effect on the number of colonies
choices.rationale: The volume of culture spread on each plate was held constant, so no trial can test its effect.

choices.text: Produce the largest possible value of the number of colonies in the experiment
choices.rationale: The 0 µg/mL row is a baseline, not an attempt to obtain a maximum.

explanation: A trial with antibiotic concentration of zero serves as the control: it establishes the baseline value of the number of colonies against which the other trials are compared.

table.caption: Experiment 1: Students spread 0.1 mL of a bacterial culture onto agar plates containing a known concentration of an antibiotic. After 24 hours they counted the colonies on each plate. Three plates were prepared for each concentration and the average count was recorded. Table 1 lists the results.

prompt: To judge the effect of the antibiotic concentration, the experimenters compared each trial with a control. Which trial was the control?

choices.text: The trial at 0 µg/mL, which received none of the treatment being tested
choices.rationale: Correct. The trial with none of the treatment shows the baseline that every other trial is compared against.

choices.text: The trial at 10 µg/mL, in the middle of the tested range of antibiotic concentration
choices.rationale: A middle value still applies the treatment; it is not a baseline.

choices.text: The trial that produced the greatest colony count
choices.rationale: A control is defined by its treatment (none), not by the size of its result.

choices.text: The trial at the greatest antibiotic concentration, 15 µg/mL, which received the most treatment
choices.rationale: The largest dose is a test condition, not the baseline.

explanation: A control receives none of the treatment: here, the trial with antibiotic concentration of 0 µg/mL.

table.caption: Experiment 1: Students spread 0.1 mL of a bacterial culture onto agar plates containing a known concentration of an antibiotic. After 24 hours they counted the colonies on each plate. Three plates were prepared for each concentration and the average count was recorded. Table 1 lists the results.

prompt: Which variable did the experimenters intentionally vary from trial to trial in Experiment 1?

choices.rationale: The glucose meter used was kept the same in every trial (a controlled variable).
The color of the plate is not part of the procedure and plays no role in the experiment.
The blood glucose level was measured as the outcome (the dependent variable).
Correct. The time after the meal was the variable the experimenters deliberately changed (the independent variable).

explanation: The procedure changes the time after the meal from trial to trial and records the blood glucose level in response, so the time after the meal is the independent variable.

table.caption: Experiment 1: A volunteer ate a measured meal after fasting overnight. A small blood sample was taken at set times afterward and its glucose concentration measured with a glucose meter. Table 1 lists the results.

prompt: In Experiment 1, which of the following was the dependent variable (the variable measured as the outcome)?

choices.rationale: The brand of the stopwatch is not part of the procedure and plays no role in the experiment.
The mass of catalyst was the variable the experimenters deliberately changed (the independent variable).
The volume of hydrogen peroxide was kept the same in every trial (a controlled variable).

choices.text: The time for the reaction to finish
choices.rationale: Correct. The time for the reaction to finish was measured as the outcome (the dependent variable).

explanation: The time for the reaction to finish is what the experimenters measured after setting the mass of catalyst, so it is the dependent variable.

stimulus.title: Catalyst and Reaction Time
stimulus.text:
Experiment 1
Students mixed 50 mL of hydrogen peroxide solution from a single bottle with a measured mass of powdered catalyst and timed how long it took for the bubbling to stop.
Results (the time for the reaction to finish): at 0 mg, 287 s; at 2 mg, 151 s; at 4 mg, 85 s; at 6 mg, 54 s; at 8 mg, 40 s.

prompt: In Experiment 1, which of the following is a controlled variable, kept the same in every trial?

choices.rationale: The brand of the speaker is not part of the procedure and plays no role in the experiment.
The distance from the speaker was the variable the experimenters deliberately changed (the independent variable).

choices.text: The height of the sound meter
choices.rationale: Correct. The height of the sound meter was kept the same in every trial (a controlled variable).
The sound intensity was measured as the outcome (the dependent variable).

explanation: Only the distance from the speaker was varied and only the sound intensity was measured; the height of the sound meter was kept the same so it could not affect the results.

table.caption: Experiment 1: In an open field, students placed a speaker playing a steady tone and used a sound meter to measure the intensity at several distances along a straight line from the speaker. Readings were taken at the same height above the ground. Table 1 lists the results.

prompt: Why did the experimenters most likely include a trial at an insulation thickness of 0 cm?

choices.text: Determine whether the room temperature has any effect on the rate of heat loss
choices.rationale: The room temperature was held constant, so no trial can test its effect.

choices.text: Produce the largest possible value of the rate of heat loss in the experiment
choices.rationale: The 0 cm row is a baseline, not an attempt to obtain a maximum.

choices.text: Check that the instrument used to measure the rate of heat loss was properly calibrated
choices.rationale: Nothing in the procedure uses the zero trial to calibrate an instrument.

choices.text: Serve as a control against which the other trials could be compared
choices.rationale: Correct. A zero trial shows what happens with none of the treatment, so the effect of each nonzero amount can be judged against it.

explanation: A trial with insulation thickness of zero serves as the control: it establishes the baseline value of the rate of heat loss against which the other trials are compared.

table.caption: Experiment 1: Students wrapped a metal box containing an electric heater in foam sheets of a set total thickness. They adjusted the heater power until the inside temperature held steady in a 20°C room and recorded that power as the rate of heat loss. Table 1 lists the results.

prompt: In Experiment 1, which of the following trials was the control trial?

choices.text: The trial that produced the greatest germination rate
choices.rationale: A control is defined by its treatment (none), not by the size of its result.

choices.text: The trial at 0 h, which received none of the treatment being tested
choices.rationale: Correct. The trial with none of the treatment shows the baseline that every other trial is compared against.

choices.text: The trial at the greatest soaking time, 16 h, which received the most treatment
choices.rationale: The largest dose is a test condition, not the baseline.

choices.text: The trial at 8 h, in the middle of the tested range of soaking time
choices.rationale: A middle value still applies the treatment; it is not a baseline.

explanation: A control receives none of the treatment: here, the trial with soaking time of 0 h.

table.caption: Experiment 1: Students soaked batches of 50 radish seeds in water for a set number of hours, then placed each batch on damp paper towels in a covered tray. After 5 days they counted the seeds that had sprouted and converted the count to a percent. Table 1 lists the results.
